races.name: Tapestry Events EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Unite John Gillespie Celebration Handicap

runners_data.name: Henery Hawk
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner dropping into a race she can control; Paul Mulrennan has placed her perfectly in recent wins at the distance, and soft going holds no concern — the 31-day break is manageable and she remains the key tactical reference point.

runners_data.name: King Of The Jungle
runners_data.note: Genuinely prominent in style, Garritty's mount arrives on a sharp upward curve with a recent Goodwood win over 5f and strong trainer form (5/31 in 14 days); the switch from good to soft is a mild unknown but course-proven and well-weighted at OR 59.

runners_data.name: Keep The Gold
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up runner who has been placed twice on good-to-soft; Lewis Edmunds holds this 4yo lightly-enough, but five furlongs soft gives minimal room for late closers and his two recent 2nds both came on faster surfaces — soft may just blunt his finish.

runners_data.name: Auntie Jo
runners_data.note: Won last time at Musselburgh over 5f on standard and has been second on the same course; runs prominently under Sam James and gets weight relief at OR 56 — the blinkers added last time appear to have sharpened her, and she is a live prominent-racing threat.

runners_data.name: Wee Mary
runners_data.note: Amie Waugh's 3lb claim is valuable here; has won and been placed on good ground recently with strong late sectionals, and the headgear (hood) likely steadies early travel — the most credible midfield finisher in the race if the pace does compress.

runners_data.name: Great Profit
runners_data.note: The youngest in the field at three, dropping back from 7f soft where she ran poorly last time; form figures on genuinely soft ground are limited and Gary Harrison has had only 0/3 in 14 days — hold-up style looks poorly suited to this tight 5f shape.

runners_data.name: Royal Duke
runners_data.note: Rhys Elliott's mount is a genuine hold-up horse placed into midfield by the weight of stay-back types in this field; Soft/SOF has seen him finish 10th previously and his last five runs all on good ground make conditions a concern — the redistribution away from his natural berth reduces his prospects.

runners_data.name: Regal Dream
runners_data.note: Tom Eaves returns this Kevin Ryan 3yo after 61 days off, and blinkers are applied; a natural closer whose recent placings all came from off the pace on good ground, but having been mapped forward from his true position at the rear, he is unlikely to find the race unfolding to his strengths on soft.

runners_data.name: Ski Angel
runners_data.note: Raced just five days ago, which is a minor freshness concern; a hold-up type who has placed at 6f on good ground but is working against herself here, being pushed out of her natural rear-running position into midfield — the Smiths have had limited recent form and 9th on soft last time is noted.

runners_data.name: Supremissy
runners_data.note: Carries a fades-in-finish flag and is a natural come-from-behind runner squeezed into midfield by the volume of hold-up horses; the two soft-ground runs in her history have produced 3rd and a poor result, and Iain Jardine's 0/3 recent strike rate further weakens the case.

runners_data.name: Bonito Cavalo
runners_data.note: A 7yo with a fades-in-finish flag and a form string of 0-0879 at Musselburgh — all recent runs have produced mid-to-rear finishes at the same course on standard going; Jim Goldie's team have been active but Bonito brings low expectations and the hold-up style is structurally disadvantaged over this trip and ground.

races.paceDynamic: Henery Hawk is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to pressure her, she will stride clear from the gates and control tempo from the front on soft ground over five furlongs at Ayr. King Of The Jungle and Auntie Jo are prominent types who will push forward and track closely, but neither is likely to fire Henery Hawk into a self-destructive gallop, leaving the overall pace manageable rather than suicidal. The soft going will place a premium on relaxed, economical travel in the first half of the race and stamina-backed finishing through the final two furlongs, rather than raw speed off a searching gallop. This race shape firmly favours front-running and close-tracking prominent types who can dictate and control their own rhythm — the hold-up brigade faces a structural disadvantage here. This field holds more hold-up types than can all find their natural position at the rear; Supremissy, Regal Dream, Royal Duke, Bonito Cavalo, and Ski Angel are all genuine closers but several will be forced to travel closer to the pace than they prefer, with Supremissy and Regal Dream the most likely to be shuffled forward by the compression of runners.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hawk Controls, Prominents Chase
scenarios.trigger: If Henery Hawk dictates an uncontested, honest gallop and the prominent pair track within striking range.
scenarios.body: If Henery Hawk dictates an uncontested, honest gallop and the prominent pair track within striking range.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Hawk
scenarios.trigger: If King Of The Jungle or Auntie Jo press Henery Hawk from early and wear her down in the soft ground before the furlong pole.
scenarios.body: If King Of The Jungle or Auntie Jo press Henery Hawk from early and wear her down in the soft ground before the furlong pole.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Hold-Up Sweeps Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses early enough for a well-positioned hold-up runner travelling strongly to pick up the pieces inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses early enough for a well-positioned hold-up runner travelling strongly to pick up the pieces inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Off Fast Pace, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If a contested early sprint creates a genuinely strong pace and the field's natural hold-up runners find a rare gap to finish through.
scenarios.body: If a contested early sprint creates a genuinely strong pace and the field's natural hold-up runners find a rare gap to finish through.

watchPoints.text: Henery Hawk's early tactical position is everything — if she is allowed to stride clear uncontested from the gate on this soft ground, she will set a rhythm very hard to overhaul in just five furlongs; watch whether King Of The Jungle or Auntie Jo seriously contest her in the first furlong.

Auntie Jo's blinkers effect has been striking since they were applied; if Sam James positions her to track Henery Hawk at the top of the field, her recent form and light weight make her a genuine threat to the leader late.

The compression of multiple hold-up types into midfield — including Supremissy, Regal Dream, and Bonito Cavalo — risks creating scrimmaging early as horses seek positions that are not available; watch for traffic issues or poor breaks from any of the redistributed runners.

Soft ground at Ayr today has been consistent across all distances per the going report; horses without a proven soft-ground profile should be treated with caution, and King Of The Jungle's only similar-going runs (2 from 15, one win, one place) are worth monitoring as a potential weakness.

Wee Mary is the only hold-up runner with genuinely recent winning form (last two runs: 1st and 2nd) and Amie Waugh's 3lb claim adds value — she is the horse most likely to outperform her price if the front rank does tire in the final furlong.

races.name: Unite Natalie Egan Celebration Handicap (For The Johnstone Rose Bowl) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Albany
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner here: Ralph Beckett sends her 289 days off the track, but her two wins both came in a lead role and she carries a style-fit note because she is technically mapped slightly out of role — however as the race's sole pace-setter she will almost certainly occupy the lead regardless, making that flag largely academic.

runners_data.name: Square Necker
runners_data.note: Won over 13f on good and placed over 12f on soft, so the 13f trip and today's conditions both stack up; Kevin Philippart De Foy is operating at a modest 1-from-19 over 14 days but this horse's recent form (31-21) is strong and Sam James is a capable handler of a race like this.

runners_data.name: Dancingwithmyself
runners_data.note: Has winning and placed form specifically over 14f on soft going — the most directly relevant soft-ground stayer in the field — and Oisin Orr's booking for Michael Bell adds a professional angle; the query is whether a 28-day absence on an already moderate recent sequence (13-243) leaves him just short of peak fitness.

runners_data.name: Oneforthegutter
runners_data.note: Out-of-form hold-up horse whose last five runs read 7-8-15-11-11 — the numbers speak plainly and soft ground over 12-16f has produced nothing in that recent sequence; Paul Mulrennan cannot manufacture form that isn't there.

runners_data.name: Peaky Blinder
runners_data.note: Won over 16f on soft and 14f on soft in back-to-back runs, giving him the strongest course-and-distance-condition profile in the field; Jason Hart takes the ride for Andrew Balding (13-from-73 over 14 days), and the hood (headgear flagged) may assist concentration on this demanding surface.

runners_data.name: Ashnak
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's 4-year-old is a natural prominent racer who on paper wants to be up with the pace, but the crowded front-running positions mean he is likely to end up racing in a more restrained role than suits him; his soft-going form is mixed (one win, one place from seven runs) and the step up to 13f is a question mark given his entire history is at 8-12f.

runners_data.name: Boatswain
runners_data.note: Simon & Ed Crisford send this horse in with no wins or places from nine soft-ground or stamina-test runs; a true prominent type who is likely to find himself unable to get his preferred position in a field of this composition, and the 0-from-23 trainer strike rate over 14 days adds further caution.

runners_data.name: Pole Star
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston runner fitted with a visor, who has raced exclusively on good ground (five career runs) — today's soft surface is a genuine unknown and represents the biggest question mark against his chance, though his form over 14-16f is consistent enough to hold an each-way claim if he handles conditions.

runners_data.name: Divine Knight
runners_data.note: William Haggas has 12 winners from 51 runners in the past 14 days but this horse has operated at 8-10f throughout his career; naturally a prominent type who is unlikely to secure that position today, and the step up to 13f on soft represents a significant unknown for a horse whose soft-ground form shows only a single place from six tries.

runners_data.name: Letsbefrank
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's local runner has won twice in recent form (1-1 in last three completed starts) over 11-12f on good, and Lauren Young's 5lb claim is useful on the handicap mark; the soft ground is a slight concern given those wins came on faster surfaces, but he is in form and travelling well enough to be monitored.

runners_data.name: Humble Spark
runners_data.note: Stablemate to Letsbefrank (Jim Goldie, Amie Waugh claiming 3lb) and ran just seven days ago — the quick turnaround is worth noting; consistent placer (442262 in current form) but all placed efforts came on good ground, and only one run on soft from 15 attempts suggests conditions may blunt her finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Alba Chiara
runners_data.note: Trainer Natalia Lupini fields this 4-year-old on the back of a win over 18f on good and a recent placed effort over 13f on good, but 16 of 19 career runs have come on good ground or faster; Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim helps a low weight, but the soft surface combined with modest recent handicap form (012-00) makes this a tough assignment.

races.paceDynamic: Albany is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only one genuine pace-setter in a 12-runner field over 1m5f on soft ground, she is likely to control proceedings at a measured, sustainable tempo — classic conditions for a horse who can dictate and be covered up by pursuers without ever being seriously pressed. Square Necker, Dancingwithmyself, Peaky Blinder, and Pole Star will push forward to track Albany, creating an orderly prominent group rather than a contested gallop. The field also contains more true prominent-running types than the race shape can accommodate: Boatswain, Ashnak, and Divine Knight are natural hold-up or tracking types by preference who are likely to find themselves shuffled further back than ideal, reducing their effective chances. A lone leader setting a soft-to-moderate pace over this distance on soft ground historically compresses the field and rewards horses who can travel prominently, conserve energy through the middle section, and quicken from a close position in the straight — the tactical verdict is clear: prominent racers who settle behind Albany and can produce a sustained finish will be most advantaged, while true hold-up horses relying on a strong enough pace to create a gap will be disadvantaged by the likely absence of that galop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Albany sets a steady, uncontested pace and the race is won by a horse tracking closely within two or three lengths throughout.
scenarios.body: If Albany sets a steady, uncontested pace and the race is won by a horse tracking closely within two or three lengths throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Albany Wins From Front
scenarios.trigger: If Albany's light weight and uncontested lead proves insurmountable and the field fails to close convincingly late on soft ground.
scenarios.body: If Albany's light weight and uncontested lead proves insurmountable and the field fails to close convincingly late on soft ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Grinder Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough early to string the field out and a durable staying type grinds past the leaders close home.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong enough early to string the field out and a durable staying type grinds past the leaders close home.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Sneaks Through
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches late and a closing horse threads through a gap to snatch late honours.
scenarios.body: If the field bunches late and a closing horse threads through a gap to snatch late honours.

watchPoints.text: Peaky Blinder has won twice on soft going over exactly this trip range (14-16f) and maps perfectly to the prominent profile that benefits from Albany's likely controlled pace — watch for Jason Hart to sit second or third and challenge entering the straight.

Pole Star has zero soft-ground experience across 12 career runs — if the ground is significantly testing he may be unable to produce his usual good-ground form, making him a fade risk despite his consistent distance profile.

Boatswain and Ashnak are both natural front-runners who are almost certainly going to be denied their preferred position by Albany and the other prominent types — watch for either to be caught wide or racing in an uncomfortable, unnatural hold-up role that markedly diminishes their chances.

Letsbefrank is a horse in form (won two of last three) for a local trainer who knows this track — Lauren Young's claim makes the weight competitive, and if the soft ground doesn't blunt him he is worth monitoring as a market mover ahead of the off.

Albany's 289-day layoff is the most significant fitness concern in the race — if she fades abruptly in the final two furlongs having led, it will open the race dramatically for the prominent chasers, particularly Square Necker and Dancingwithmyself who have the soft-ground form to capitalise.

races.name: Dalcon Civil Engineering Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Lanarra
runners_data.note: Placed twice in soft going including a win at Sandown, this 3yo filly has genuine soft-ground credentials at 6-7f; Oisin Orr provides a useful booking and the 12-day freshener suits, though 7f is the outer edge of her form distances — a natural hold-up runner who will need a clear run late.

runners_data.name: Lope Y Linda
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 3yo returns just 4 days after her last run which is unusually quick and invites a fitness query; her soft-going form is limited to longer trips and David Allan will need to produce her late in what figures to be a sprint finish — has yet to win but has placed on good ground over this trip.

runners_data.name: Queenies Pal
runners_data.note: Headgear (tongue-pin) noted and trainer Noel Wilson has a quiet 14-day record; soft-going form shows a third at 6f but her wider form is modest — she will race closer to the pace than her true hold-up nature dictates in this field, meaning she's operating partially out of her comfort zone.

runners_data.name: Royal Baroness
runners_data.note: Mike Smith's filly has three soft-ground runs to her name without a win, and the claim of Rhys Elliott (5lb) is a slight negative in a competitive sprint finish; her redistribution onto the pace-map means she'll be closer than ideal for a horse that has never won — form in soft has been consistent but unspectacular.

runners_data.name: Approaching Dawn
runners_data.note: Ran just yesterday which is an extreme quick turnaround and Lauren Young (5lb) is a young claim on a 6yo who has soft-going form limited to a single run; Jim Goldie's 7/44 14-day trainer strike rate is reasonable, but the fitness question after back-to-back racing days looms large and she carries top weight at 135lbs.

runners_data.name: Ridgemaster
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Standard ground and has placed at 6f on good; Amie Waugh (3lb claim) rides for her trainer-father Simon Waugh and that combination is a tight unit — carrying 135lbs is a concern and soft going is untested, but if a jockey is going to push forward and steal this, Ridgemaster's win over 7f gives her some tactical versatility.

runners_data.name: Ring Of Gold
runners_data.note: A 9yo with a 7f placed effort on Standard to his name; form figures of 225407 show consistency without a win and the soft going is a factor for a veteran — Billy Garritty takes over and the horse, while a natural hold-up type, will operate in a pack of similarly styled rivals with limited scope for improvement.

runners_data.name: Trais Fluors
runners_data.note: Linda Perratt's 12yo Trais Fluors has the oldest legs in the field and form has been poor across recent starts (548850); Tom Eaves is an experienced handler of hold-up horses in sprint finishes at tracks like Ayr, but the age and recent form make it very hard to make a case — soft going does not feature prominently in recent history.

runners_data.name: Evelyn's Garden
runners_data.note: Tagged as a horse that fades in the finish — a serious concern in what is expected to be a late-sprint shape; Katie Scott's 3yo has zero wins in 5 starts and soft-going form shows an eighth, so the combination of the fade flag and limited soft credentials make this a horse to pass over even in a competitive race like this.

runners_data.name: Monhammer
runners_data.note: Veteran of 8yo with four soft-going runs showing two placings at 7f; Linda Perratt again here, and Paul Mulrennan is an astute Ayr jockey who knows when to switch his mount forward — the horse will sit closer to the pace than his natural style prefers in this field, and that positional adjustment could actually help if the race is a muddled sprint.

runners_data.name: No Nay Nevermind
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's 4yo has soft-going form that shows a sixth at 6f and little else of note in similar conditions; Andrew Mullen takes the ride and the horse carries 135lbs, which combined with limited soft-going evidence makes this a tough ask — will be pushed forward out of necessity rather than design in this hold-up-heavy field.

runners_data.name: Pebble Dash
runners_data.note: Headgear (p) noted and four consecutive fourths suggest consistency without the ability to win; Barry McHugh rides Gary Harrison's 4yo who has one soft-going run in recent history — the monotonous placing record is both a reliability signal and a ceiling indicator, and in a sprint finish this horse may find the same position as always: fourth.

races.paceDynamic: This 7f soft-ground contest at Ayr is a rare race where every single runner in the field carries a hold-up profile, meaning there is no natural front-runner to set a genuine gallop and the field is almost certain to dawdle into a muddling, compressed sprint finish off a slow early pace. Without any horse wanting to commit to the front, the field will likely crawl through the early stages, bunching tightly, before the pace explodes in the final two furlongs — a pattern that historically favours horses with a late burst over soft ground at this trip. This chaotic, slow-run scenario significantly reduces the advantage of superior form and raises the chance of positional luck, track position from the widest or narrowest draw, and raw finishing pace on soft ground becoming decisive. Hold-up horses who can get a clear run in the sprint finish — particularly those with soft-going form and a reliable turn of foot — are best positioned, though the compressed nature of the field means that getting daylight late will be the critical differentiator. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically all sit at the rear; of those likely to push forward out of necessity or instinct, Queenies Pal, Monhammer, and No Nay Nevermind are the horses most plausible to drift closer to the pace than their natural style suggests.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow burn sprint finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field drifts into a crawl early and the race ignites in the final two furlongs with a wall of horses charging together.
scenarios.body: If the field drifts into a crawl early and the race ignites in the final two furlongs with a wall of horses charging together.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Soft-ground hold-up gallop
scenarios.trigger: If one or two horses break from the hold-up pack and set a modest but genuine pace, giving real hold-up runners a target to aim at.
scenarios.body: If one or two horses break from the hold-up pack and set a modest but genuine pace, giving real hold-up runners a target to aim at.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-thief steals it
scenarios.trigger: If a jockey seizes the initiative from a wide or favourable draw and pinches a lead, controlling the tempo unchallenged.
scenarios.body: If a jockey seizes the initiative from a wide or favourable draw and pinches a lead, controlling the tempo unchallenged.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic chaos undoes all
scenarios.trigger: If the bunched sprint finish produces sustained interference, with hold-up horses blocking each other in the straight.
scenarios.body: If the bunched sprint finish produces sustained interference, with hold-up horses blocking each other in the straight.

watchPoints.text: With no front-runner in the field, watch for a complete false pace scenario in the early stages — any horse that drifts to the front by accident or design before the 4f marker could steal an uncontested lead; Ridgemaster and No Nay Nevermind are the most plausible to drift forward.

Approaching Dawn ran yesterday and carries 135lbs in soft ground — monitor any signs of fatigue or reluctance in the paddock and early stages, as a tired horse in a tightly bunched field creates significant interference risk for those around her.

Monhammer's jockey Paul Mulrennan is a seasoned Ayr handler who may force the horse forward out of its natural hold-up role to secure position in a sprint finish — if Mulrennan commits early, it changes the tactical picture for every horse behind him.

Evelyn's Garden is flagged as a horse that fades in the finish and is mapped out of her natural position; in a field of twelve that will bunch late, a fading runner in the pack is a danger to others — Jason Hart will need to be alert to avoid a collision in the closing stages.

The draw could matter more than form in this race — with twelve hold-up horses running in a sprint finish on soft ground, those drawn widest have the clearest unobstructed run to the line and may gain a positional advantage that has nothing to do with ability.

races.name: Unite George Ramsay Celebration EBF Land O'Burns Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Beautiful Diamond
runners_data.note: Top-rated soft-ground performer with two wins in similar conditions, set to lead on a track and trip she handles well; races slightly out of her usual prominent role stepped up to lead, but the tactical context suits her and Sam James keeps things simple.

runners_data.name: Billie Be Quick
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type returning just six days after her last run, wore a hood today and Paul Mulrennan can deliver her late; soft going is fine but her form string shows a preference for good ground and she has rarely threatened in similar company.

runners_data.name: Fluorescence
runners_data.note: Won on good-to-soft but her recent form is patchy; a natural front-runner who is mapped to midfield because the field is overloaded with pace types, meaning she may be forced to settle against her instincts with Oisin Orr needing to adapt the ride.

runners_data.name: Kinswoman
runners_data.note: William Haggas-trained filly returning from a 14-day break with just one soft-ground run on her card, that a second; she wants to race prominently but with several others chasing the same early position, Harry Davies may not get the berth he needs.

runners_data.name: Layla Liz
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's filly is a three-time winner on standard-to-slow surfaces and hits the track after 55 days off, but her natural style is prominent rather than the hold-up role she's been mapped to given the congested pace picture.

runners_data.name: Luna A Inbhir Nis
runners_data.note: Local trainer Katie Scott fields her at OR 96 and she gets 5f Ayr on soft ground; her sim-going record shows zero wins from three outings on soft, and she has missed the frame on good at Ayr twice — the class is there but conditions remain unproven.

runners_data.name: Rhyme Dust
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's filly has been consistent in soft conditions across 6f but drops to 5f here, and that trip-switch on a pulling track like Ayr in soft is a legitimate query; her recent form string shows no wins from ten starts, so finishing late but not winning is her pattern.

runners_data.name: Rose Of Honour
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in three career starts, all at 6f on good or standard surfaces; the drop to 5f and step up to soft ground are both unexplored, yet her trainer James Tate sends her here with confidence and she has been freshened over 49 days.

runners_data.name: Sapphire Princess
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's filly drops sharply in trip from her last two 7f starts and hasn't run in 250 days; she races naturally up with the pace but the fitness question after such a long absence is acute, and the redistribution to midfield may actually suit an underdone runner.

runners_data.name: Argentine Tango
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's three-year-old has been consistently placed but has not won in six starts; her soft-ground record of zero wins from three tries does not encourage, and her form line of 4466 suggests she finds a way to be involved without winning.

runners_data.name: Cardiff By The Sea
runners_data.note: Won last time on soft ground at 5f showing she handles conditions; a keen front-runner by nature who is mapped to midfield because the position is overcrowded, but Andrew Slattery may push forward to reclaim her natural berth given the recent win here.

runners_data.name: Coconut Cove
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's filly has a single soft-ground run and finished fifth; Jack Mitchell will ride positively but she prefers 6f and the trip may find her out before she can use her class in the closing stages on this surface.

runners_data.name: Shes Got A Brother
runners_data.note: A double winner this season but both victories came on standard surfaces at 5f; wears a hood and Billy Garritty holds an aggressive brief, yet with the field full of prominent types she will have to earn her position — her inexperience at Listed level is the key unknown.

runners_data.name: Thenandnow
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on soft at Dundalk and handles soft well; mapped to midfield despite wanting to race up with the pace, dropping to 5f at Ayr is a test of a different kind and her trainer's 14-day strike rate of 5/29 is solid if she travels to Ayr primed.

runners_data.name: Thora
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's second string returns after 104 days off the track, last seen finishing fifth; her two wins came on standard turf over 6f and the combination of a long absence, first run on soft, and a 5f trip she has never won at makes her an appealing watch-and-wait runner.

races.paceDynamic: Beautiful Diamond is the one confirmed front-runner and, with the field containing so many prominent-types competing for early position, she is likely to set a straightforward, sustainable gallop from the off without being seriously pressured for the lead itself. However, the sheer volume of horses wanting to race prominently — Kinswoman, Cardiff By The Sea, Fluorescence, Sapphire Princess, Thora, Shes Got A Brother and Thenandnow among others — means there will be fierce jostling for the positions just behind her, creating a genuinely competitive pace scenario through the first two furlongs on soft ground. The soft going at Ayr will ensure this pace takes its toll, rewarding horses who travel efficiently rather than those who burn energy fighting for positions they cannot naturally hold. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate: of those redistributed to midfield, Cardiff By The Sea, Fluorescence and Kinswoman are the most likely to press forward and actually secure a prominent berth. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape favours horses with genuine class and an ability to settle just off the pace or hit the line strongly from midfield, with soft-ground efficiency at 5f the decisive filter.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest but not chaotic, and the strongest prominent-types travel powerfully to strike at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: If the pace is honest but not chaotic, and the strongest prominent-types travel powerfully to strike at the two-furlong pole.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Slog Rewards Class
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is truly strong enough that front-runners and over-eager prominent types are taken off their legs by the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the early pace is truly strong enough that front-runners and over-eager prominent types are taken off their legs by the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Gifts It
scenarios.trigger: If Beautiful Diamond faces minimal pressure and dictates an overly moderate gallop, turning the race into a sprint finish from halfway.
scenarios.body: If Beautiful Diamond faces minimal pressure and dictates an overly moderate gallop, turning the race into a sprint finish from halfway.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Storms Home Late
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution causes traffic problems throughout the pack, creating a scrambled mid-race with late closers finding a clear run only in the dying strides.
scenarios.body: If the redistribution causes traffic problems throughout the pack, creating a scrambled mid-race with late closers finding a clear run only in the dying strides.

watchPoints.text: Cardiff By The Sea and Kinswoman are both natural front-runners squeezed into midfield on the map — if either breaks sharply and forces their way to a prominent berth, it will unsettle the pace calculations and drag Beautiful Diamond into a faster-than-expected duel.

Rose Of Honour is unbeaten but has never encountered soft ground or a 5f trip; a visibly uneasy surface or signs of greenness in the first furlong would be a significant red flag that her odds do not yet reflect.

Sapphire Princess returns from 250 days off the track — watch the market move and the paddock demeanour closely, as a well-backed runner here who looks sharp would suggest connections are confident despite the fitness concern.

Beautiful Diamond's STYLE_FIT tag means she is racing outside her fully natural role; if she shows any sign of over-racing or fighting for the lead rather than controlling it, the pace dynamic could unravel and the entire scenario A probability shifts downward.

The going report confirms consistent soft ground across all Ayr races today — horses who have not proven their ability on soft (Rose Of Honour, Billie Be Quick on good, Layla Liz on artificial) should be monitored through the first two furlongs for any loss of rhythm or reluctance to handle the surface.

races.paceDynamic: Napolian is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner 7f Ayr handicap on Soft ground, and with no obvious challenger for the lead, Mark Winn can dictate terms at whatever tempo suits from the front. The Soft going will naturally compress the pace, making it harder for hold-up horses to generate the sustained momentum needed to close significant gaps — a horse controlling proceedings from the front on this surface is well-placed. This field is loaded with genuine hold-up types: Circle Of Trust, Ellie's de Vega, Sanny Doo, Horace Wallace, and Blue Mantle are all natural closers, but there are far too many of them to occupy true rear positions, meaning several will be shuffled into midfield roles that do not suit their natural style. The race shape strongly favours a horse who can race prominently or in the slipstream of Napolian — prominent racers who travel close to the frugal pace are best-positioned to pounce, while the glut of displaced hold-up types must produce a finish they are not ideally configured for.

watchPoints.text: Napolian sets an uncontested frugal gallop — if Mark Winn is never headed through the first four furlongs, the race may be effectively over for the large hold-up contingent trying to make up ground on a soft, energy-sapping surface.

Milford Grange has the strongest Soft-ground placing record in the field (3 from 4 on Soft) — watch whether Billy Garritty positions it closer than its natural style suggests, as a prominent pitch here would make it the most dangerous rival to the leader.

The cluster of five redistributed hold-up types (Circle Of Trust, Ellie's de Vega, Sanny Doo, Horace Wallace, Blue Mantle) all competing for midfield positions creates significant traffic risk entering the straight — a straightforward run through is not guaranteed for any of them.

Storm Esme's trainer Tim Easterby is in top form (8 winners from 104 runners over 14 days) — monitor market moves, as a yard operating at that level hitting the board with an OR-70 runner that has Soft-ground experience is worth noting even if the tactical profile is not ideal.

Real Jack's unknown running style is a genuine wildcard — if Paul Mulrennan elects to push forward early and takes up a prominent position, it would add unexpected pressure to Napolian and materially change the race shape from a controlled to a contested lead scenario.

races.paceDynamic: Eternal Sunshine is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 14-runner field on soft ground at Ayr, and with no genuine rival willing to press for the early lead, she is set to control the pace from the outset at a tempo she can dictate entirely on her own terms. Behind her, Parisiac is the only other natural prominent type, likely to track in second or third, while the vast majority of the field are true hold-up horses who will be shuffled back in a convoy. On soft ground over 6f at Ayr, an uncontested lead with a sustainable gallop is a significant tactical advantage — the pace will be honest but not punishing, meaning Eternal Sunshine can conserve energy through the first two furlongs before stretching rivals in the final stages. Several horses are tagged as redistributed from their true hold-up role into midfield on the map — Aberama Gold, Abduction, Oriental Prince, Dandy Magic, Lion's House, Kelpie Grey, Whiskey Kisses and Falcon Queen are all natural closers who cannot all operate from their preferred rear position in this shape, with only those drawn or travelling widest likely to secure meaningful separation. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape strongly favours the prominent/front-running profile, with hold-up horses facing the double jeopardy of soft ground and a field so packed with closers that clean passage from the rear will be fiercely contested.

watchPoints.text: Eternal Sunshine must be tracked from the stalls — if she breaks cleanly and crosses to the front unchallenged, she dictates the entire shape of this race and the prominent profile is immediately in control.

Parisiac's ability to sit second to Eternal Sunshine without being headed by a redistribution horse early is crucial — watch whether any of the Goldie stable runners (Abduction, Oriental Prince) try to push forward and compromise the projected race shape.

Roberto Caro is the hold-up horse with the strongest soft-ground credentials in the field — if the pace collapses in the final furlong he is the closer most likely to be finishing fastest, and Mikey Sheehy's positioning from the gate bears watching.

Jim Goldie saddles four runners (Eternal Sunshine, Abduction, Oriental Prince, Kelpie Grey) — with a trainer strike rate of 7/44 in 14 days, watch whether any of the lesser-fancied stablemates are ridden with unexpected intent to create pace complications.

Soft ground on the day is confirmed for this 6f contest — horses with zero or limited soft-ground experience (Novamay, Whiskey Kisses, Falcon Queen) should be assessed cautiously, as the going report suggests conditions are consistent and testing throughout the card.
